method_note: All sources have stable IDs bound to exact URLs. Evidence notes are bounded paraphrases, not copied page captures. Do not silently rebind IDs. Fictional-service facts are from the assigned brief, not external sources.

sources.title: Testing the useability and applicability of Australian multilingual public service communications
sources.release_version_or_commit: 61-page public report title page says June 2023. RMIT project page separately lists project dates April 2023–June 2024; exact final report release date is not otherwise stated.
sources.locator: PDF pp. 10–14: methods, language groups, respondents and survey process; pp. 15–18: method/document preference and exceptions; pp. 19–20: respondent reasons; project page identifies commissioning body and study frame.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RMIT University project page and 61-page linked report through the web reader; inspected methods, demographics, four-method preference tables, and stated limitations.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Commonwealth Department of Health and Aged Care commissioned a study of four COVID-19 public-health documents, translated by four methods into seven languages. It used 21 community readers (three per language) recruited across Australian states; focus groups/survey were in each respondent’s preferred language, oral or written. Four versions of each of four documents were considered in sequence with a 77-question survey. Methods 3 (Plain-English source rewrite then double human translation) and 4 (direct target-language drafting from a brief) were preferred on three documents; the fourth webpage document favored conventional translation and method 3 drew the most confusion, with font/layout/wording explanations.
sources.applicability_and_transfer_limit: The report is a useful multilingual implementation comparison because it reports audience, language, recruitment intent, tasks, language assistance, and preference/confusion outcomes. Its 3-per-language cells, sequential subjective ratings, sample skew (including Australian education and English information use), lack of objective comprehension/task-completion tests, and health-message domain limit inference. It does not choose a best method for a community-course notice or establish the center’s policy.
